Findings.Title: Kerberoastable Accounts
Findings.Description: Enabled user accounts with a Service Principal Name (SPN) can have a Kerberos service ticket requested and cracked offline (Kerberoasting).
Findings.Recommendation: Use Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA) or enforce AES-only, long/random passwords for service accounts.

Findings.Title: Kerberoastable Accounts Permitting RC4
Findings.Description: Kerberoastable accounts still permitting RC4-HMAC encryption are dramatically faster to crack offline than AES-only accounts.
Findings.Recommendation: Set msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes to AES-only (24) on all service accounts.

Findings.Title: AS-REP Roastable Accounts
Findings.Description: Accounts with Kerberos pre-authentication disabled allow an AS-REP message to be requested and cracked offline.
Findings.Recommendation: Enable Kerberos pre-authentication on all accounts unless a specific, documented exception applies.

Findings.Title: Unconstrained Kerberos Delegation
Findings.Description: Accounts/computers trusted for unconstrained delegation can cache and replay the Kerberos TGT of any user that authenticates to them.
Findings.Recommendation: Migrate to constrained delegation or Resource-Based Constrained Delegation (RBCD); remove unconstrained delegation unless strictly required.

Findings.Title: KRBTGT Password Age
Findings.Description: The krbtgt account signs and encrypts all Kerberos tickets in the domain and should be rotated regularly.
Findings.Recommendation: Reset the krbtgt password (twice, several hours apart, following the documented procedure) at least every 180 days.

Findings.Title: AdminSDHolder Orphaned Accounts
Findings.Description: Accounts with adminCount=1 that are no longer members of a protected group keep an inherited restrictive ACL and are easy to overlook during access reviews.
Findings.Recommendation: Review and, where appropriate, reset adminCount and restore ACL inheritance on these accounts.

Findings.Title: Protected Users Group Adoption
Findings.Description: The built-in Protected Users group provides additional Kerberos-based protections for Tier 0 administrative accounts.
Findings.Recommendation: Evaluate adding Tier 0 administrative accounts to the Protected Users group where operationally feasible.

Findings.Title: LDAP Server Signing
Findings.Description: LDAPServerIntegrity controls whether the LDAP server requires signing of incoming LDAP binds.
Findings.Recommendation: Set LDAPServerIntegrity to 2 (Required) on all Domain Controllers.

Findings.Title: LDAP Channel Binding
Findings.Description: LdapEnforceChannelBinding controls whether LDAP binds over SSL/TLS require a channel binding token, protecting against LDAP relay attacks.
Findings.Recommendation: Set LdapEnforceChannelBinding to 2 (Always) on all Domain Controllers.
